results.notes:
I made no edits; this is the same blocker W1-18 reported. When I started, the owned files had no uncommitted changes. HEAD already holds S8-A (executor park, resume, run_parked frame, RunParked 24 and RunResumed 25, chat-client handling, TTL expiry, spare of parked and resuming folds) and the session-core half of S8-B (crash park behind SESSION_CORE_CRASH_PARK_ENABLED, default off). The only work left is the executor half of S8-B. None of it can be built without unowned files, and the park-key source guard forbids the shortcut through agent.rs.

(1) Markers on round folds. The worker refuses every crash-park candidate as route_unrecorded until the executor writes parks-so-far, route model, connection id and child ceiling on round folds of run_parkable loops. `fold::build_fold` makes fresh extensions each time. The four keys are written only in `park::park_fold`, and `tests/durable_loop_contract.rs` (lines ~1498-1515) fails if agent.rs, or park.rs outside `park_fold`, names any of them. So the writer has to be a new function in park.rs, called from the round-save site in agent.rs (`folds.save_round(fold)`, about line 4206 in the loop-end block), with the guard amended and mutation rows added.

(2) Zombie stop. `FoldWriter` lets agent.rs ask only `is_failed()`, which is also true for a store that refused the run for good (`SaveError::Refused`). Stopping on every failed writer would change flag-on behaviour for runs that are not zombies. It needs an accessor in fold.rs that is true only for a Stale or Closed save.

(3) The thread_watermark P1 from W1-18 (a stale stamp closing a legitimate later park) is not reachable with the code as built. `build_fold` and `park_fold` make fresh extensions, so a resumed executor never carries the stamp into a later fold. Only session-core's own re-seal of a crash park and the round-fold stamp in `save()` write that key, and `save()` overwrites it. Nothing needs to change in loop_checkpoint.rs, so I changed nothing. The finding can be downgraded to P3, with a source guard on `build_fold` if wanted.

depth_findings.text: Until sse.rs calls run_tool_rounds_for_model_with_attachments, turning CHAT_SANDBOX_ATTACHMENTS_ENABLED on makes AttachmentPolicy accept kind:file attachments that nothing stages: files would be silently dropped. Keep the switch off until the sse.rs shared edit is in.
Kernel read-only enforcement (EROFS on writes into attachments/, nested ro-bind inside the writable bind) and removal of the 0555 directory are unproven on Linux: the bwrap tests skip on Windows.

Persistent Space roots: staging reuses StagedInputs there and removes the directory afterwards, but no test covers a persistent root, and the assumption that the reserved name attachments is free in Space workspaces (WS22 exclusion, WS19 skills) is unverified.

RunInputs is keyed (org_id, run_id) and shared by all steps of a run, so a concurrent code_interpreter step of the same run with no attachments can also read the registered files; same run authority, S6 (Do) should decide whether that is intended.

The sandbox note is appended as the last system message of the tool-round prompt on a turn with files, which breaks prompt-cache prefix stability only for those turns; WS02 prompt ordering may want a fixed position.
No db or live test of the zdr row for code_interpreter staging beyond the existing zdr_feature_table file-attachment row; the executor refusal is unit-tested but not through a real gRPC server.

Zeroing in run_inputs is a plain fill plus black_box because unsafe is forbidden and no zeroize crate is a dependency; copies in the workspace file and gRPC request buffer are not zeroed. Adding zeroize needs a Cargo.toml change.

Per-file and total caps in mp-contracts (8 MiB each, 16 MiB total, 8 files) are ceilings above the gateway's declared 1 MB / 3 MiB / 3 files so a cap raise (OD18) is configuration only; align with decode limit headroom when WS08-S7 lands.
toStreamAttachments reads getAttachmentPolicy() at call time, so a turn composed before the catalogue loaded sends no file bytes; the server then sees only inlined text, the safe direction.

Edits outside the owned list: execution-core/src/lib.rs and model-gateway/src/lib.rs (one pub mod line each, unavoidable for the new modules), model-gateway/src/browser_run.rs (attachments: Vec::new() in a struct literal, compile necessity), model-gateway/src/zdr_posture.rs (CALL_SITES row renamed to run_tool_rounds_for_model_with_attachments) and tests/context_recovery_contract.rs (re-pointed after the entry-point split). Each is minimal and forced by the design; the lead should accept them explicitly or relocate them.

Persistent Space roots: StagedInputs::stage calls remove_staged_dir(root/attachments), whose set_mode(dir, 0o755) follows symlinks. A program in an earlier call of the same run can plant attachments as a symlink to a host path, and the next staging call chmods the target as the execution-core user (the existing program-file write has the same symlink-following exposure). Before enabling staging for Space-bound turns, check symlink_metadata and unlink a non-directory entry without chmod. The same function also deletes a legitimate Space file or directory named attachments (reserved-name assumption, no test).

CHAT_SANDBOX_ATTACHMENTS_ENABLED is read by sandbox_staging_enabled() but nothing calls it yet (sse.rs pending), while attachment_policy.rs already publishes modes.sandbox_files from the same variable, so the FE would send file bytes that the server drops. The switch must stay off until the sse.rs hand-off lands.

Kernel read-only enforcement (EROFS for both an existing file and a new file in attachments/), the 0555 directory removal on Drop, and the argv order (ro-bind after the writable --bind) are only unit-tested on argv shape here; the behavioural bwrap tests skipped on Windows and need the Linux container run.

Plan row names a golden (code_interpreter staging, ZDR) in zdr_feature_table.rs and a log-redaction test; neither was added. The ZDR and waived refusal is covered only by unit tests of register_step_attachments and handle_code_interpreter, not through a real gRPC server.

RunInputs is keyed (org_id, run_id) and shared by every code_interpreter step of the run, so a concurrent step of the same run that carried no attachments can still read the registered files; S6 (Do) must decide whether that is intended. A repeat registration of a run silently keeps the first list (the later steps' lists are ignored).

The sandbox note is pushed as the last system message of the tool-round prompt only on turns with files, so prompt-cache prefix stability is lost for those turns; WS02 prompt ordering may want a fixed slot.

Zeroing is fill(0) plus black_box on the registry copy only; the gRPC request buffer, the workspace file and the gateway's RunAttachment copies are not zeroed (no zeroize dependency). Also the ZDR/waived check in execute_step uses req.zdr || caller.zdr || caller.zdr_waiver, while the gateway-side handle_code_interpreter checks only zdr (execution-core is the backstop).
